title: Constant subsheaf quotient stalk isomorphism
statement: Let X be a topological space and iota:K -> C a monomorphism of abelian sheaves, where C is isomorphic to the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Fix n,b in N, opens A_i (i in Fin n), labels 0 < c_i <= b+1, and an epimorphism g from the finite coproduct of j_{A_i!}Z [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero] to K. Suppose its i-th component sends the canonical unit section to s_i in K(A_i), and iota(s_i) is the constant c_i under the given isomorphism of C. Let f have component g_i for c_i <= b and zero otherwise, L=image(f), l:L -> K the image inclusion, U=union_i A_i and V=union_{c_i<=b} A_i. Assume L has zero stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] outside V. For any q:j_{U!}Z -> cokernel(l) whose unit section on each top-labelled A_i maps to the image of s_i under the cokernel projection, the stalk map q_x is an isomorphism at every x in U outside V. The lemma assumes q and its section values and asserts no existence of q.

proof.text: Choose an index i active at x from membership in iSup A. The exclusion from V and upper bound on labels force c_i=b+1.
Use integer coordinates for the unit germ of the source extension and the quotient germ of s_i.

Apply the stalk map germ formula and the given q section compatibility to identify the image of the source generator with the quotient generator. An additive map between groups with unique integer generator coordinates is bijective: represent two source elements for injectivity and a target element for surjectivity. Mathlib ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective then yields IsIso.

proof_origin.place: Final paragraph: explicit unit germ compatibility and integer-coordinate bijectivity proof.
